title: Partners
purpose: Every hour goes to the client through the same spine. It does not matter who runs the floor. So a partner's site is as safe to sell as our own site.
how: We have two channels, and both use the same spine. The first channel is direct operations: our own team, with about 135 phones, in factories and warehouses. The second channel is delivery partners: they run about 135 of our phones with their own people, in hotels in four cities, in Mansoura, and on their own sites. In total we have about 270 phones. The client sees one company.

The spine is the set of rules that every channel shares. No channel may skip any of them. Every wearer goes through onboarding screening. Every person has one account, in their own name, and KMSC creates it. We review every video before the client sees it. We pay for accepted hours, minus the hours with fraud flags. A channel is the way we reach a floor. The spine is what makes the hours worth buying.

The founders agree every partnership. Adham owns the contract. Mano does the paperwork. Moharam works with the partner day to day. Mano handles the money. Partners are not on the org chart, and that is on purpose. Their people are not KMSC staff, and they never contact the client.

There is one agreement, with seven terms, and it is the same for every partner. One: pay for accepted hours, minus fraud flags. Two: the partner must follow the spine to be paid. Three: our phones stay under MDM, with custody and return rules. Four: the partner must upload footage every day. Five: the partner must follow our data-protection rules. Six: we can audit the partner. Seven: either side can exit within 7 days, with a device count. Nobody changes a term when they are out with a partner. If a partner asks for a different deal, that is a warning sign about the partnership.

A partner is paid the same way we are paid. The client pays for accepted hours after the month-end audit. We count a partner's hours the same way, from the QC verdicts and the wearer log, and we take off flagged footage first. If a device count is still open, we hold the payment. If the amount is above the threshold, Adham signs as the second person. Partner rates are written in the agreement and nowhere else.

How to choose the channel for a new site. If we have people on the bench, and the site has fiber or a hub close by, we run it as direct operations. If someone already runs the floor and will take our phones and our spine, they are a partner operator. If someone has their own sites and people, and wants to deliver hours to our standard, they are a delivery partner. In all three cases, the gate is ours. Moharam certifies the site before any hour counts. Moharam does this only after Mano confirms every wearer file and Mano confirms the count.

procedures.name: Signing a new partnership
procedures.owner: Adham, with Mano on the paperwork
steps: Walk through the partner's floors. Count the phones the sites need. Confirm the upload path. Write down the task categories that these sites add.
Sign the standard agreement. Nobody changes the seven terms when they are out with a partner. Only Adham can change a term.
Write down the payment terms with Mano. Tell both sides that Moharam is the day-to-day contact.
No phone leaves the store until the agreement is signed and the first site has a plan.

procedures.name: Handing phones to a partner
steps: Enroll every phone before it leaves. Put it in Apple Business Manager and Hexnode. Set it to supervised. Put the collection app in kiosk mode. Check that the phone shows on the map.

Hand over complete kits, one kit for every ten phones, with a phone list. At the handover, the person who hands over the phones signs, and the person who receives them signs. The same day, write the partner as the custodian in the registry.
Write the upload path in the site plan. It is one of two things: the partner's own line, tested at 100 Mbps sustained or better, or a hub that runs under our transport rules.
On the partner's floor, run one 30-minute test session on every phone. Confirm that the footage uploads.

procedures.name: Onboarding a partner's wearer
procedures.owner: Mano owns the gate. Mazen runs it at the partner's launch day. Moharam certifies.
steps: The partner names the person. KMSC activates the person. We copy the ID. The person must be 18 or older. The person signs the consent form in Arabic, and we explain it in person.
We give the fraud briefing, and the wearer signs it. KMSC creates one account, in the wearer's name.
Write the wearer in the wearer log: name, device number, site, and start date.
Fit the rig. Check the angle. Review the first 30 minutes of footage before the wearer films the next 30 minutes.
If there is no paperwork, there is no account. If there is no account, no hours count.

procedures.name: Monthly partner payment
steps: After the month-end audit, get the accepted hours for each partner from the QC verdicts and the wearer log.
Take off the flagged footage first. Hours on a shared account count as zero. Hours on an account with no paperwork count as zero.
Check the registry. If any device count is still open, hold the payment until the count matches.
If the amount is above the threshold, Adham signs as the second person. Then pay the partner, on the same cycle as site payments.

procedures.name: Partner audit
steps: Do the audit at the partner's premises every quarter, and on any day Moharam asks. Count the phones and compare the count with the registry and the MDM.
Compare the wearer log with the gate files. Every name must have an ID copy, a consent form, and a signed fraud briefing.
Walk the floor. Check the angle on each wearer's head. Check the signs at the entrances. Check that sensitive areas are marked off.
If the count does not match, investigate the same day. If there is still no explanation after 24 hours, put the missing phones in lost mode, and tell Adham that night.

procedures.name: A flag at a partner site
steps: Send the flag to Moharam and the partner the same day. Include the session ID and say exactly what the wearer must correct.
The partner corrects the wearer within 24 hours and tells Moharam it is done.
On the second strike, the device is paused until the wearer is retrained. On the third flag, the wearer is removed. That wearer is never enrolled again, under any name or on any device.
Flagged hours are taken off the invoice first, and then off the partner's payment.

procedures.name: Ending a partnership
procedures.owner: Adham decides. Moharam and Mano run the exit.
steps: Either side can give notice in writing, for any reason. If we give notice, Adham sends it. If the partner gives notice, it goes to Moharam, and Moharam sends it to Adham and Mano the same day. The 7 days start on the day the notice is received.
Every phone is flushed before it travels. Every phone, mount, and charger comes back within 7 days, and we count them against the registry.
Close every account. Never use an account again for anyone else. Collect the wearer log.

We pay when the count matches. If a phone is not back on day 7, put it in lost mode that day. There are 24 hours to get the phone back. After that, wipe the phone, file a police report, and update the registry.

breaks.what: A partner's wearer filmed but never passed the gate
breaks.do: Take the device off the wearer right away. Moharam confirms this within the same hour. Youssef Medhat holds every session from that device and does not send any of them. Tell Mano the same day. Those hours are not paid. Moharam checks every wearer on that site again before filming starts again.

breaks.what: A partner site is holding more than one device-day of footage
breaks.do: This is an incident, the same as on our own sites. Tell Moharam the same day. The partner uploads all the footage tonight on their own line. That is their duty under the agreement. If the line cannot do it, our runner takes one third of the phones per run to the nearest hub, under the transport rules. Or Mano fixes the line. No phone stays full overnight on anyone's premises.
Hold the payment until the count is done. The agreement says this, and it is there for exactly this case. Moharam tells Adham the same day.

breaks.what: A partner stops answering, or leaves with our devices
breaks.do: First, find the phones with MDM. Put them in lost mode within the hour. There are 24 hours to get them back. After that, wipe the phones, file a police report, and update the registry. Hold all payments. Tell Adham the same night. The 7-day exit period starts.

No hour on the shared account is paid, and the account is closed. The partner puts every wearer on that site through the gate again before filming starts again. If it happens a second time, Adham decides whether the partnership continues.

breaks.what: A partner, or one of their workers, names the client or contacts the client
breaks.do: Moharam pauses filming at that site within the hour. Adham handles everything to do with the client. The agreement calls this a breach. Adham decides the same day whether the partnership continues.

breaks.what: A phone with footage on it is lost at a partner site, or a clip leaks
breaks.do: Tell Moharam and Mano within the hour. Mano brings in the lawyer. Put the phone in lost mode within the hour. Adham calls the client within 24 hours. Mano and the lawyer tell the regulator within 72 hours. This is why the partner must tell us within the hour, not within the day. The agreement says so.

breaks.what: A partner says the accepted-hours count is wrong
breaks.do: The same day: Moharam checks the facts, Mano checks the money, and Adham checks the contract. The record is the QC verdicts and the wearer log. The month-end audit is final. Hold the payment while any device count is open. Nobody is paid for an hour the client did not accept. That includes us.

training: Moharam and Mano learn the seven terms and what each one is for. They spend one afternoon with Adham. This happens before their first talk with a partner.

Partner floor leads take the operator day-one module. It takes two hours, and Mazen teaches it at their first launch day. It covers the rig, the angle, the 30-minute cycle, the rule that hat off means tap stop, and custody.
Partner wearers get the same fraud briefing as our own wearers. It is in Arabic and in person. The wearer signs it before the first shift.
Mano learns the partner handover, the phone list, and custody. This is part of the one-day training with Mano.

questions.q: Why do we put our phones on a partner's floor instead of using the partner's phones?
questions.a: Because the phone is how we keep control. It has MDM, kiosk mode, the map, and the wipe. On their phones, we would have to trust what they tell us. On our phones, we have the count.

questions.q: A partner already has trained people. Do they still go through the gate?
questions.a: Yes. Every wearer in every channel goes through the gate. That means the ID copy, the consent form, the fraud briefing, one account, and the wearer log. A trained person is not the same as a person with the right paperwork.

questions.q: What does a partner get paid?
questions.a: The rate is in their agreement and nowhere else. It is not on this site and not in a chat. The way we pay is public: accepted hours, minus fraud flags, after the audit.

questions.q: Can a partner talk to the client?
questions.a: Never. Not the partner's owner, not their floor lead, and not a wearer. Anything to do with the client goes to Moharam first, and then to Adham.

questions.q: The delivery partners are independent. What does that mean?
questions.a: They run their own floors, their own people, and their own uploads. They do not run their own screening, accounts, review, or count. Those things are the spine, and the spine is ours.

partners.name: Direct operations
partners.model: KMSC staff use KMSC phones, and we run the whole spine ourselves

partners.name: Delivery partners
partners.where: Hotels in four cities, Mansoura, and their own sites
partners.model: Their sites and their people, with our phones and our standards. Central planning sets the number of phones for each site

agreement.term: Pay for accepted hours, minus fraud flags
agreement.text: The partner is paid for the hours the client accepts. Payment comes after the month-end audit. Flagged footage is taken off first. This is the same way we are paid. Nobody is paid for an hour the client did not accept.

agreement.term: The partner must follow the spine to be paid
agreement.text: Every wearer goes through the gate. That means we copy the ID, the wearer is 18 or older, the wearer signs the consent form, the wearer signs the fraud briefing, the wearer has one account in their own name, and the wearer is written in the wearer log. Every video goes through our review. Hours on an account with no paperwork, or on a shared account, count as zero.

agreement.term: Our phones stay under MDM, with custody and return rules
agreement.text: The phones belong to Vound, even when they are on the partner's premises. They are enrolled and supervised, the collection app is in kiosk mode, and they show on the map at all times. At the handover and at every transfer, the person who hands over the phones signs, and the person who receives them signs. Phones stay at the site, at a hub, or in a case that someone has signed for. They never go to anyone's home.

agreement.term: The partner must upload footage every day
agreement.text: The partner uploads the footage from every phone every day. They use their own line, tested at 100 Mbps sustained or better, or a hub that runs under our transport rules. No phone keeps more than one day of footage overnight. If a site holds more than one device-day of footage, that is an incident.

agreement.term: The partner must follow our data-protection rules
agreement.text: The partner must follow the same data-protection rules that we follow. Get consent before filming. Put signs at the entrances. Do not film in restrooms, locker rooms, prayer rooms, clinics, or offices. Do not upload through anyone's home. If a phone is lost, a clip leaks, or someone complains, the partner tells Moharam and Mano within the hour. Then Adham can tell the client within our 24-hour limit.

We can go to the partner's premises, count the phones, read the wearer log, check the gate files, and walk the floor. We do this every quarter, and on any day Moharam asks. If the partner refuses an audit, we hold the payment until the count is done.

agreement.term: Either side can exit within 7 days, with a device count
agreement.text: Either side can end the partnership, in writing, for any reason. Within 7 days, every phone, mount, and charger comes back, and we count them against the registry. All accounts are closed and never used again. We pay when the count matches.
